Both objects exist and are set up as requested. The rule is enabled and its last run succeeded.

**Dashboard: "EFF-9df6ad4d Web logs overview"** (ID `8f6a0e0c-ce3a-4c7c-85e7-29bf414375c1`, last 7 days)
- Metrics: Total requests (count), Unique visitors (unique count of `clientip`), Total bytes served (sum of `bytes`)
- Requests over time (line, ES|QL)
- Responses by status code (bar, ES|QL on `response.keyword`)
- Requests by OS (bar, ES|QL on `machine.os.keyword`)
- A markdown note describing the data and the linked alert

**Alert rule: "EFF-9df6ad4d 5xx spike"** (ID `a6b6d74c-0eb6-4085-8687-eeaeeafb6870`, enabled)
- Type: Elasticsearch query (KQL) on the Kibana Sample Data Logs data view
- Query: `response.keyword >= "500" and response.keyword <= "599"`
- Count of matching docs over a 5-minute window, `>` threshold of 10, checked every 1 minute
- No connector actions, so it only records alerts and sends no notifications. Add one if you want notifications.

**What I explored in the data view**
- Time field: `timestamp`. `@timestamp` has the same range.
- Key fields: `response` (status code, string), `bytes`, `clientip`, `geo.dest`, `machine.os`, `extension`, `url`/`request`, `agent`.
- Status codes: 200 (12,832), 404 (801), 503 (441). The 5xx slice is all 503s, which is 441 documents in total.

**Things to know**
- The rule has not fired yet (last run: 0 alerts). I could not confirm whether any 5xx documents fall in the current 5-minute window.
- The sample timestamps run from 2026-10-04 to 2026-12-03, so part of the dataset is in the future relative to today (2026-10-11). That may affect when the rule sees data.
- Kibana's console and ES|QL REST routes are disabled in this environment, so I checked the data through Kibana's internal ES|QL route and the rule's run status. I did not query Elasticsearch directly.
- I did not verify the dashboard panels by rendering them in the UI; I confirmed them through the API only.
